notes: s013 could be headed on 'evil' if kakologeo were read as a support-verb frame, but both English words gloss an element of the compound, so rule 66's core clause applies and rule 91's 'speaking evil of' precedent heads the verb word.
Both articles before 'father' and 'mother' take the supplied 'thy' under rule 20's second arm, no genitive pronoun standing to displace them.
The 'of' at t015 stands over an accusative object and is the verb's own phrasal government under rule 106's accusative arm.
